Imperative_EN: [ONE-SHOT-GUIDANCE: ADD_TIAB] In initial query construction, include tiab synonyms in FILTER for variant spellings and abbreviations not covered by MeSH. Pair tiab terms with MeSH equivalents where possible: ("TERM"[Mesh] OR "TERM"[tiab]). Do not use tiab as sole coverage for core CONDITION or INTERVENTION slots. NAMED-INSTANCES RULE: When a slot contains a broad category concept (e.g., Biomarkers, Antihypertensive Agents, Diagnostic Techniques, Pathogens) AND the paper involves specific named instances of that category (e.g., specific protein names, specific drug names, specific gene variants, antibiotic brand/class names), add those specific instance names as tiab terms. BROAD FALLBACK FLOOR: Always keep the broad class MeSH and at least one broad tiab alongside the specific names - never replace broad coverage with only a named list. Example: ("Biomarkers"[Mesh] OR biomarker*[tiab] OR CRP[tiab] OR ESR[tiab]) is correct; (CRP[tiab] OR ESR[tiab]) alone is incorrect. INTERVENTION VARIANT COVERAGE: For intervention classes with many historical variants (antibiotics, biologics, antiseptics), include generation names, brand names, class names, and broad class terms. Wildcard (antibiotic*, biologic*) covers unknown variants.

Apply this action ONLY when the term being removed is a LITERAL synonym or abbreviation/expansion pair - e.g., 'TB' when 'tuberculosis' is already present, or vice versa. CRITICAL: Do NOT treat a narrower (more specific) term as redundant merely because a broader category term is present. Training-data evidence: removing 'GLP-1 Receptor Agonists'[Majr] on the grounds that 'Hypoglycemic Agents'[Majr] already covered it caused a measurable recall loss - papers describing GLP-1 receptor agonists did not always use the broader category label. The same applies to any hyponym/hypernym pair (e.g., a specific biomarker vs 'biomarker', a specific drug vs its drug class, a specific symptom vs 'symptom'). When in doubt, KEEP the specific term.
